long_title: An Act to incorporate a teaching and residential Muslim University at Aligarh.
preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to incorporate a teaching and residential Muslim University at Aligarh, and to dissolve the Societies registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860), which are respectively known as the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, and the Muslim University Association, and to transfer to and vest in the said University all properties and rights of the said Societies and of the Muslim University Foundation Committee; It is hereby enacted as follows:

sections.title: Short title and commencement
sections.text: (1) This Act may be called the Aligarh Muslim University Act, 1920. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint. [Brought into force on 1st December, 1920.]

sections.title: Definitions
sections.text: In this Act and in all Statutes made hereunder, unless the context otherwise requires: (a) 'Academic Council' means the Academic Council of the University; (b) 'Board of Studies' means the Board of Studies of the University; (c) 'Chancellor', 'Pro-Chancellor' and 'Vice-Chancellor' mean respectively the Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor of the University; (d) 'Court' means the Court of the University; (e) 'Department' means a Department of Studies and includes a Centre of Studies established by the Ordinances; (f) 'Executive Council' means the Executive Council of the University; (g) 'Faculty' means a Faculty of the University; (h) 'Hall' means a unit of residence or of corporate life maintained by the University for its students; (hh) 'non-teaching staff' means the employees of the University other than the teachers; (i) 'Statutes', 'Ordinances' and 'Regulations' mean respectively the Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations of the University for the time being in force; (k) 'Teachers' means Professors, Readers, Lecturers and such other persons as may be appointed for imparting instruction in the University or a hall and are designated as Teachers by the Ordinances; (l) 'University' means the educational institution of their choice established by the Muslims of India, which originated as the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, and which was subsequently incorporated as the Aligarh Muslim University.

sections.title: Incorporation
sections.text: The Chancellor, the Pro-Chancellor and the Vice-Chancellor and the members of the Court, the Executive Council and the Academic Council, for the time being, shall be a body corporate by the name of the Aligarh Muslim University and shall have perpetual succession and a common seal and shall sue and be sued by that name.

sections.title: Dissolution of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, and the Muslim University Association, and transfer of all property to the University
sections.text: From the commencement of this Act: (i) the Societies known as the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, and the Muslim University Association shall be dissolved, and all property, movable and immovable, and all rights, powers and privileges of the said Societies and of the Muslim University Foundation Committee shall be transferred to and vest in the University; (ii) all debts, liabilities and obligations of the said Societies and Committee shall be transferred to the University and shall thereafter be discharged and satisfied by it; (iii) all references in any enactment to either of the said Societies or to the said Committee shall be construed as references to the University; (iv) any will, deed or other document containing any bequest, gift or trust in favour of either of the said Societies or of the said Committee shall be construed as if the University was named instead; (v) subject to any orders which the Court may make, the buildings which belonged to the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, shall continue to be known and designated by their former names and styles; (vi) every person employed immediately before the commencement of this Act in the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, shall hold employment in the University by the same tenure and upon the same terms and conditions and with the same rights and privileges as to pension and gratuity as he would have held under the College.

sections.title: Powers of the University
sections.text: The University shall have the following powers, namely: (1) to provide for instruction in such branches of learning as it may think fit, and to make provision for research and for the advancement and dissemination of knowledge; (2)(a) to promote Oriental and Islamic studies and give instruction in Muslim theology and religion and to impart moral and physical training; (b) to promote the study of the religions, civilisation and culture of India; (c) to promote especially the educational and cultural advancement of the Muslims of India; (3) to hold examinations and to grant diplomas or certificates to, and confer degrees and other academic distinctions on, persons subject to such conditions as the University may determine, and to withdraw the same for good and sufficient cause; (4) to confer honorary degrees or other distinctions in the manner laid down in the Statutes; (5) to provide instruction for persons who are not members of the University, as it may determine; (6) to co-operate or collaborate with other Universities and authorities; (7) to institute professorships, readerships, lectureships and other teaching or academic posts and to appoint persons thereto and determine their conditions of service in accordance with the Statutes; (7A) to appoint persons working in any other University, institution or organisation as teachers of the University for a specified period; (8) to institute and award fellowships (including travelling fellowships), scholarships, studentships, exhibitions and prizes in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances; (9) to institute and maintain Halls for students; (9A) to establish within a radius of twenty-five kilometres of the University Mosque such Special Centres, Specialised Laboratories or other units for research and instruction as are necessary; (10) to demand and receive such fees and other charges as may be prescribed by the Ordinances; (11) to supervise and control the residence and regulate the discipline of students, and to make arrangements for promoting their health; (11A) to make special arrangements in respect of the residence, discipline and teaching of women students; (11B) to create administrative, ministerial and other posts and make appointments and determine their conditions of service in accordance with the Statutes; (11C) to regulate and enforce discipline among employees and take disciplinary measures; (11D) to acquire, hold, manage and dispose of property, movable or immovable, including trust or endowed property; (11E) to borrow, with the approval of the Central Government, on the security of the property of the University, money for the purposes of the University; (11F) to declare a Department of Studies to be an autonomous Department; (12) to do all such other acts and things whether incidental to the powers aforesaid or not as may be requisite to further the objects of the University.

sections.title: Recognition of degrees
sections.text: The degrees, diplomas and other academic distinctions granted or conferred by the University shall be recognised by the Central and State Governments as are the corresponding degrees, diplomas and other academic distinctions granted by any other University incorporated under any enactment.

sections.title: Reserve fund
sections.text: The University shall invest and keep invested in securities in which trust funds may be invested, in accordance with the law relating to trusts in India, a sum of thirty lakhs of rupees as a permanent endowment to meet the recurring charges of the University other than charges in respect of fellowships, scholarships, prizes and rewards, subject to provisos regarding valuation of Government securities and reduction of the sum by the capitalised value of certain permanent recurring grants and income from certain transferred immovable property.

sections.title: University open to all persons
sections.text: The University shall be open to all persons (including the teachers and taught) of either sex and of whatever race, religion, creed, caste or class: Provided that nothing in this section shall be deemed to prevent religious instruction being given in the manner prescribed by the Ordinances to those who have consented to receive it.

sections.title: [Omitted]
sections.text: Formerly related to religious instruction. Repealed by the Aligarh Muslim University (Amendment) Act, 1951 (62 of 1951), s. 6.

sections.title: Residence of students
sections.text: Every student of the University shall reside either in a Hall or a hostel or under such conditions as may be prescribed by the Ordinances.

sections.title: Teaching in the University
sections.text: All recognised teaching for the purpose of University degrees, diplomas and certificates shall be conducted under the supervision of the Academic Council and in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances.

sections.title: Power to establish and maintain High Schools and other institutions
sections.text: (1) The University shall, subject to the Statutes, have power to establish and maintain High Schools within a radius of fifteen miles from the University Mosque. (2) The University may also, with the sanction of the Visitor and subject to the Statutes and Ordinances, establish and maintain such Special Centres, Specialised Laboratories or such other institutions for research or instruction as are necessary, either on its own or in co-operation or collaboration with any other institution.

sections.title: [Omitted]
sections.text: Formerly 'Power to recognise colleges and institutions'. Repealed by the Aligarh Muslim University (Amendment) Act, 1972 (34 of 1972), s. 9, w.e.f. 17-6-1972.

sections.title: The Visitor
sections.text: (1) The President shall be the Visitor of the University. (2) The Visitor shall have the right to cause an inspection to be made of the University, its buildings, laboratories, equipment, and of any institution maintained by it, and of examinations, teaching and other work conducted or done by the University, and to cause an inquiry into any matter connected with the administration or finances of the University. (2A) The Visitor shall give notice to the University of his intention to cause an inspection or inquiry, and the University may make representations. (2B) After considering any representation, the Visitor may proceed with the inspection or inquiry. (2C) The University may appoint a representative to be present and heard at such inspection or inquiry. (3) The Visitor may address the Vice-Chancellor with reference to the result of such inspection/inquiry, and the Vice-Chancellor shall communicate the Visitor's views and advice to the Executive Council. (4) The Executive Council shall communicate to the Visitor, through the Vice-Chancellor, action proposed or taken. (5) Where the Executive Council does not act to the Visitor's satisfaction within a reasonable time, the Visitor may, after considering any explanation, issue directions with which the Executive Council shall comply. (6) The Visitor may, by order in writing, annul any proceeding of the University not in conformity with this Act, the Statutes or the Ordinances, after calling upon the University to show cause. (7) The Visitor shall have such other powers as may be prescribed by the Statutes.

sections.title: [Omitted]
sections.text: Formerly 'The Visiting Board'. Omitted by the Aligarh Muslim University (Amendment) Act, 1951 (62 of 1951), s. 11.

sections.title: Chief Rector
sections.text: The Governor of the State of Uttar Pradesh shall be Chief Rector of the University.

sections.title: Officers of the University
sections.text: The following shall be officers of the University: (1) The Chancellor; (2) The Pro-Chancellor; (3) The Vice-Chancellor; (3A) The Pro-Vice-Chancellor, if any; (3B) The Honorary Treasurer; (3C) The Registrar; (3D) The Finance Officer; (3E) The Deans of the Faculties; and (4) such other officers as may be declared by the Statutes to be officers of the University.

sections.title: The Chancellor
sections.text: (1) The Chancellor of the University shall be elected by the Court in such manner and for such term as may be prescribed by the Statutes. (2) The Chancellor shall, by virtue of his office, be the Head of the University. (3) The Chancellor shall, if present, preside at the convocations of the University held for conferring degrees.

sections.title: The Pro-Chancellor
sections.text: (1) The Pro-Chancellor shall be elected by the Court in such manner and for such term as may be prescribed by the Statutes. (2) The Pro-Chancellor shall, in the absence of the Chancellor, preside over the convocations of the University held for conferring degrees.

sections.title: The Vice-Chancellor
sections.text: (1) The Vice-Chancellor shall be appointed by the Visitor in such manner as may be prescribed by the Statutes. (2) The Vice-Chancellor shall be the principal executive and academic officer of the University, and shall exercise general supervision and control over the affairs of the University and give effect to the decisions of all the authorities of the University. (3) The Vice-Chancellor may, where immediate action is necessary, exercise any power conferred on any authority of the University and shall report the action taken to such authority, subject to a right of reference to the Visitor by the authority and a right of appeal to the Executive Council by any aggrieved person in the service of the University. (4) The Vice-Chancellor shall exercise such other powers and perform such other functions as may be prescribed by the Statutes or Ordinances.

sections.title: The Pro-Vice-Chancellor
sections.text: The Pro-Vice-Chancellor shall be appointed in such manner, and shall exercise such powers and perform such duties, as may be prescribed by the Statutes.

sections.title: The Honorary Treasurer
sections.text: (1) The Honorary Treasurer shall be elected by the Court in such manner and for such term as may be prescribed by the Statutes. (2) The Honorary Treasurer shall exercise such powers and perform such functions as may be prescribed by the Statutes.

sections.title: The Registrar
sections.text: (1) The Registrar shall be appointed in such manner as may be prescribed by the Statutes. (2) The Registrar shall have the power to enter into agreements, sign documents and authenticate records on behalf of the University and shall exercise such other powers and perform such other duties as may be prescribed by the Statutes.

sections.title: The Finance Officer
sections.text: The Finance Officer shall be appointed in such manner and shall exercise such powers and perform such duties as may be prescribed by the Statutes.

sections.title: Powers of other officers
sections.text: The powers of officers other than the Chancellor, the Pro-Chancellor, the Vice-Chancellor, the Pro-Vice-Chancellor, the Honorary Treasurer, the Registrar and the Finance Officer shall be prescribed by the Statutes.

sections.title: Authorities of the University
sections.text: The following shall be the authorities of the University: (1) The Court; (2) The Executive Council; (3) The Academic Council; (3A) The Finance Committee; (3B) The Faculties; and (4) such other authorities as may be declared by the Statutes to be authorities of the University.

sections.title: The Court
sections.text: (1) The Court shall consist of the Chancellor, the Pro-Chancellor, the Vice-Chancellor and the Pro-Vice-Chancellor (if any), and such other persons as may be specified in the Statutes. (2) The Court shall be the supreme governing body of the University and shall exercise all the powers of the University not otherwise provided for by this Act, the Statutes, the Ordinances and the Regulations, and shall have power to review the acts of the Executive and Academic Councils (save where such Councils have acted in accordance with powers conferred on them). (3) Subject to this Act, the Court shall: (a) make Statutes and amend or repeal the same; (b) consider Ordinances; (c) consider and pass resolutions on the annual report, annual accounts and financial estimates; (d) elect persons to serve on the authorities of the University and appoint officers as prescribed; and (e) exercise such other powers and duties as conferred or imposed by this Act or the Statutes.

sections.title: The Executive Council
sections.text: The Executive Council shall be the principal executive body of the University. Its constitution, term of office of members, and its powers and duties shall be prescribed by the Statutes.

sections.title: The Academic Council
sections.text: (1) The Academic Council shall be the principal academic body of the University and shall, subject to this Act, the Statutes and the Ordinances, co-ordinate and exercise general supervision over the academic policies of the University. (2) The constitution of the Academic Council, term of office of its members, and its powers and duties shall be prescribed by the Statutes.

sections.title: Other authorities of the University
sections.text: The constitution, powers and functions of the Finance Committee and of the Faculties, and of such other authorities as may be declared by the Statutes to be authorities of the University, shall be prescribed by the Statutes.

sections.title: Disqualifications for membership
sections.text: A person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of any of the authorities of the University if he is not a citizen of India.

sections.title: Power to make Statutes
sections.text: Subject to this Act, the Statutes may provide for: (a) the constitution, powers and functions of the authorities of the University and such other authorities as may be constituted from time to time; (b) the election and continuance in office of members of the said authorities, filling of vacancies, and other related matters; (c) the manner of election or appointment of the Chancellor, the Pro-Chancellor, the Vice-Chancellor and other officers; (d) the manner of appointment of teachers and other academic staff and their emoluments; (e) the manner of appointment of employees other than teachers and academic staff and their emoluments; (f) the manner of appointment of teachers/academic staff from other institutions for joint projects; (g) conditions of service of employees including pension, insurance, provident fund, termination and disciplinary action; (h) principles governing seniority; (i) procedure for arbitration in disputes between employees or students and the University; (j) procedure for appeal to the Executive Council against action of any officer or authority; (k) establishment and recognition of Students Union or associations of teachers/staff; (l) all other matters which by this Act are to be, or may be, provided by the Statutes.

sections.title: Statutes
sections.text: (1) On the commencement of the Aligarh Muslim University (Amendment) Act, 1981, the Statutes then in force, as amended, shall be the Statutes of the University. (2) The Court may make new or additional Statutes or amend/repeal existing Statutes as provided in this section. (3) The Executive Council may propose to the Court the draft of any Statute, subject to prior consultation with any authority whose status, powers or constitution is affected. (4) The Court may approve, reject, or return the draft for reconsideration with suggested amendments. (5) Any member of the Court may propose a draft Statute, subject to the same procedure via the Executive Council. (6) No new Statute or amendment/repeal shall come into force unless approved by the Visitor, who may sanction, disallow, or return it for further consideration.

sections.title: Power to make Ordinances
sections.text: (1) Subject to this Act and the Statutes, Ordinances may provide for: (a) admission of students and enrolment; (b) courses of study for degrees, diplomas and certificates; (c) award of degrees/diplomas/certificates and qualifications therefor; (d) fees for courses, admission, examinations, degrees and diplomas; (e) conditions for award of fellowships, scholarships, studentships, exhibitions, medals and prizes; (f) conduct of examinations including examining bodies, examiners and moderators; (g) remuneration of examiners, moderators, invigilators and tabulators; (h) conditions of residence of students; (i) special arrangements for residence, discipline and teaching of women students; (j) religious instruction; (k) emoluments and terms of service of academic and other staff; (l) maintenance of high schools and other institutions under section 12; (m) establishment of various Centres, Boards, Committees etc.; (n) manner of co-operation/collaboration with other Universities; (o) creation of bodies for improving academic life; (p) other terms and conditions of teachers not prescribed by Statutes; (q) all other matters which may be provided for by Ordinances. (2) Ordinances in force before the 1972 Amendment Act may be amended, repealed or added to by the Executive Council, acting on recommendation of the Academic Council except for matters in clauses (k) and (p). (3) The Executive Council cannot amend a draft proposed by the Academic Council but may reject or return it for reconsideration with suggested amendments. (4) Where rejected/returned, the Academic Council may reaffirm the original draft by the prescribed majority, and it shall be sent back to the Executive Council, which shall adopt it or refer it to the Visitor whose decision is final. (5) Every Ordinance made by the Executive Council shall come into effect immediately. (6) Every Ordinance shall be submitted to the Visitor within two weeks; the Visitor may direct suspension of its operation within four weeks and, after receiving comments, either withdraw the suspension or disallow the Ordinance, his decision being final.

sections.title: Regulations
sections.text: (1) The authorities of the University may make Regulations consistent with this Act, the Statutes and the Ordinances for: (a) procedure at meetings and quorum; (b) matters to be prescribed by Regulations under this Act, the Statutes or Ordinances; (c) other matters solely concerning such authorities or committees not otherwise provided for. (2) Every authority shall make Regulations for giving notice of meetings and business, and for keeping records of proceedings. (3) The Executive Council may direct amendment or annulment of any Regulation made under this section other than one made by the Court. (4) Every Statute, Ordinance or Regulation made under this Act shall be published in the Official Gazette. (5) Every Statute, Ordinance or Regulation shall be laid before each House of Parliament for thirty days, which may modify or annul it (without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under it).

sections.title: [Omitted]
sections.text: Formerly 'Admission to the University'. Repealed by the Aligarh Muslim University (Amendment) Act, 1951 (62 of 1951), s. 23.

sections.title: Examinations
sections.text: (1) All arrangements for the conduct of examinations shall be made, and all examiners appointed by the Executive Council on the recommendation of the Academic Council. (3) The Academic Council shall appoint examination committees, consisting of members of its own body or other persons or both, to moderate examination questions and to prepare and publish results of examinations.

sections.title: Annual report
sections.text: (1) The Annual Report of the University shall be prepared under the direction of the Executive Council and submitted to the Court on or after such date as prescribed by the Statutes, and the Court shall consider it at its annual meeting. (2) The Court shall submit the Annual Report to the Visitor and the Chancellor along with its comments, if any. (3) A copy of the Annual Report as submitted to the Visitor shall also be submitted to the Central Government, which shall cause it to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.

sections.title: Annual accounts
sections.text: (1) The annual accounts and balance sheet shall be prepared under the direction of the Executive Council and audited at least once every year (intervals not exceeding fifteen months) by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India or his authorised representative. (2) A copy of the annual accounts and audit report shall be submitted to the Court and the Visitor along with the Executive Council's observations. (3) Any observations of the Visitor shall be brought to the Court's notice, and the Court's observations, after consideration by the Executive Council, submitted to the Visitor. (4) A copy of the annual accounts and audit report as submitted to the Visitor shall also be submitted to the Central Government, which shall cause it to be laid before both Houses of Parliament. (5) The audited annual accounts, after being laid before Parliament, shall be published in the Gazette of India.

sections.title: Conditions of service of employees
sections.text: (1) Every employee of the University shall be appointed on a written contract, lodged with the University, with a copy furnished to the employee. (2) Any dispute arising out of a contract between the University and any employee shall, at the employee's request, be referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration consisting of one member appointed by the Executive Council, one nominated by the employee, and an umpire appointed by the Visitor. The Tribunal's decision is final and no suit shall lie in any Civil Court in respect of matters so decided; provisions of the Indian Arbitration Act, 1899 (except section 2) apply accordingly.

sections.title: Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students
sections.text: (1) A student or examination candidate removed from the rolls by order of the Vice-Chancellor, Discipline Committee or Examination Committee, and debarred from examinations for more than a year, may appeal to the Executive Council within ten days of receipt of the order, and the Executive Council may confirm, modify or reverse the decision. (2) Any dispute arising from disciplinary action against a student shall, at the student's request, be referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration, with section 36(2) applying as far as possible.

sections.title: Right to appeal
sections.text: Every employee or student shall have a right to appeal, within such time as prescribed by the Statutes, to the Executive Council against the decision of any officer or authority, and the Executive Council may confirm, modify or reverse the decision appealed against.

sections.title: Provident and pension funds
sections.text: (1) The University shall constitute, for the benefit of its officers, teachers and servants, such pension or provident funds or insurance schemes as it deems fit, in accordance with the Statutes. (2) Where such a fund is constituted, the Central Government may declare that the Provident Funds Act, 1925, shall apply to it as if it were a Government provident fund.

sections.title: Filling of casual vacancies
sections.text: Casual vacancies in any office or in any authority shall be filled up by the authority which has power to appoint to the office or authority.

sections.title: Proceedings of University authorities not invalidated by vacancies
sections.text: No act or proceeding of any authority of the University shall be invalidated merely by reason of the existence of a vacancy or vacancies among its members.

sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith
sections.text: No suit or other legal proceeding shall lie against any officer or employee of the University for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of the provisions of this Act, Statutes or Ordinances.

sections.title: Mode of proof of University record
sections.text: A copy of any receipt, application, notice, order, proceeding, resolution of any authority or Committee of the University, or other documents in possession of the University, or any entry in any register duly maintained by the University, if certified by the Registrar, shall be received as prima facie evidence of such document or entry and shall be admitted as evidence of the matters and transactions therein where the original would have been admissible, notwithstanding anything in the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, or any other law for the time being in force.

sections.title: The Schedule
sections.text: For the Statutes of the University, see the University Calendar.
